tasks.title: Entry-tier winter promo sitting on the knife edge
tasks.user_request: We want a simple winter offer on the entry wireless product to get some volume moving. Take the 50/12.5 Mbps from R1,299 down to R1,199 for the 90-day window, new customers, 12-month agreement, back to R1,299 afterwards. Finance flagged that our published margin on that product is comfortable, so this should be fine, but please confirm properly and show me the working - I don't want to take a hand-wave to the board.
tasks.inputs: Product: Tarana FWB 50/12.5 Mbps. Standard retail R1,299/month ex-VAT. Wholesale/access MRC R499/month. Proposed promotional price R1,199/month for 90 days. Contract term 12 months. Reversion R1,299/month. Installation cost R2,550 per customer, one-off, amortised over the first 12 months of the 12-month agreement. Per-subscriber recurring charges available to you: Static IP R50, BNG R30.30 (Tier 1, R20.20 at 1,000+ subs), IP Transit R28, Backhaul R86, Support R30, BSS R10.96. The published product-economics 'All-in Cost' for this tier is R817/month. All figures ex-VAT. Governing commercial rules: .claude/rules/margin-guardrails.md and .claude/rules/product-economics.md.
coverage: verdict_basis_rule - highest-cost defensible reading
verdict flips between cost bases
sensitivity analysis kept separate from verdict
least favourable volume tier when base size unstated
charge applicability not positively excluded must be included
shortfall quantification on a near-miss
assumption disclosure does not excuse a favourable basis

evaluation_packet.what_success_means: The verdict is FAIL, computed on the R946.50 build-up, with the ~R63/month shortfall quantified. The R817 published all-in cost - which the requester has effectively pre-endorsed - is either rejected as the verdict basis or shown only as labelled sensitivity. This is the single most discriminating task in the suite: the entire difference between a pass and a fail is which cost basis is chosen.
objective_facts: Standard cost build-up used across this benchmark (highest-cost defensible reading, ex-VAT, per subscriber per month): wholesale/access MRC for the SPEED TIER ACTUALLY DELIVERED + Static IP R50 + Cost-of-Sale floor at the LEAST FAVOURABLE applicable subscriber-base tier (R185 at 100 users = BNG R30.30 + Transit R28 + Backhaul R86 + Support R30 + BSS R11; R182 at 300; R179 at 1,000; R175 at 1,500+) + installation amortisation R2,550/12 = R212.50 (the rules doc rounds this to R213; the R0.50 difference moves any margin by <0.05pp and flips no verdict). This yields Tarana all-in R946.50 (50/12.5), R1,046.50 (100/25), R1,146.50 (200/50). The published 'All-in Cost' column in product-economics.md (R817 / R917 / R1,017) is R129.50 LOWER than this build-up and is a lower-cost reading. It is separately inconsistent with its own stated component list by R24 (R499+50+30+28+11+10+213 = R841, not R817; the same R24 gap holds on all three rows), and it carries a single R28 line where the Cost-of-Sale floor table charges Transit R28 PLUS Backhaul R86, and Support R10 where the floor table charges R30. Per the contract's verdict_basis_rule the verdict must be computed on R946.50/R1,046.50/R1,146.50; R817/R917/R1,017 and the R841 literal-component reading may appear only as labelled sensitivity analysis.

SUBSCRIBER BASE IS NOT SUPPLIED. Per the verdict_basis_rule the least favourable applicable volume tier must be used: the 100-user COS row, R185. Choosing R175 (1,500+ users) without evidence of that base size is an assumption that favours the offer and is disallowed. (It does not rescue the offer anyway - see below - but choosing it is still a verdict-basis error.)
VERDICT COST BASIS: R499 wholesale + R50 static IP + R185 COS floor (100-user row, least favourable) + R212.50 install amortisation (R2,550/12) = R946.50/subscriber/month.

VERDICT: FAIL. 21.06% is below the 25% non-negotiable floor. It sits in the '< 25% - CFO approval (rarely granted)' band and is above the 20% 'Never permitted' line, so it is theoretically survivable only with CFO approval, which must be named rather than assumed.

SHORTFALL: minimum compliant price = R946.50 / 0.75 = R1,262.00. Shortfall = R1,262.00 - R1,199 = R63.00 per subscriber per month. In percentage points: 25% - 21.06% = 3.94 pp. Over the 90-day promo, 3 x R63.00 = R189.00 per subscriber of margin below the floor.

THE FLIP - THIS IS THE POINT OF THE TASK. Using the published 'All-in Cost' R817: margin = (R1,199 - R817)/R1,199 = R382/R1,199 = 31.86% - a comfortable PASS in the 25-35% 'Marginal / Sales Director' band. Using the literal component list from the same doc (R499+50+30+28+11+10+212.50 = R840.50): margin = R358.50/R1,199 = 29.90% - also a PASS. Using the mandated build-up: 21.06% - a FAIL. Only the highest-cost defensible reading (R946.50) may determine the verdict, so the correct answer is FAIL. Any answer that returns PASS has failed the contract's rank-1 quality, and disclosing 'we used the published all-in cost' does not cure it - the assumption_disclosure_rule states disclosure never substitutes for choosing the highest-cost defensible basis.

WHY R946.50 IS DEFENSIBLE AND HIGHEST: product-economics.md's Cost of Sale Floor table explicitly instructs 'Excludes access costs (Tarana/DFA wholesale) - add those per product', i.e. R185 + R499. The published R817 is internally inconsistent with its own component list (which sums to R841) and charges only R28 transit where the COS floor table charges R28 transit PLUS R86 backhaul, and R10 support where the floor table charges R30. R946.50 > R840.50 > R817, so R946.50 is the highest of the three defensible readings.

SECOND-ORDER TRAP - STATIC IP: if a contestant drops the R50 static IP without positively excluding it, cost = R896.50 and margin = R302.50/R1,199 = 25.23% - a bare PASS by 0.23 pp. The verdict_basis_rule requires inclusion of 'every per-service and per-subscriber charge whose applicability is not positively excluded'. Nothing in the inputs excludes static IP, so it must be included and the verdict is FAIL. A PASS obtained this way is a rank-1 failure, not a rounding difference.

VOLUME-TIER SENSITIVITY (does not change the verdict): at the 1,500+ COS tier R175, cost = R936.50 and margin = R262.50/R1,199 = 21.89% - still a FAIL. The flip is driven by the cost-basis choice, not the volume tier. A contestant that only sensitises volume tier and declares the offer robust has tested the wrong variable.

DISCOUNT AND APPROVAL: (R1,299 - R1,199)/R1,299 = R100/R1,299 = 7.70%, inside the 5-10% Sales Director band (24-month max, non-DFA - satisfied). Promotional pricing separately requires MD pre-approval. But because the post-discount margin is 21.06%, margin-guardrails.md's 'All discounts must maintain the 25% minimum margin floor' overrides the band: the discount cannot be granted at Sales Director level regardless of its size. Correct routing: CFO (sub-25% margin) at minimum, plus MD pre-approval for the promotional mechanic - or, preferably, reprice.
CORRECT REMEDY if the promo must run: price at R1,262.00 or above (a 2.85% discount off R1,299, inside Sales Rep authority, 25.00% margin exactly). At R1,269 the margin is 25.41%.

REQUIRED OPERATIONAL FIELDS: duration 90 days (at the cap); eligibility new customers; contract term 12 months; reversion R1,299/month (at which the margin is R352.50/R1,299 = 27.14% on the verdict basis - itself only marginal, worth flagging).

TOLERANCE: figures within R1.00 or 0.1 percentage points of those stated are equivalent. The supplied per-subscriber line items sum to R185.26 while the published cost-of-sale floor table states R185, and the install amortisation is R212.50 against the rules doc's rounded R213; neither rounding flips any verdict.
evaluation_packet.relative_importance: Rank 1 (verdict on the highest-cost defensible basis) overwhelmingly dominates and is effectively the whole task. Rank 3 (assumptions consistent with figures) is second: a contestant may state 'assuming the published all-in cost' and be internally consistent yet still fail, because the contract forbids a favourable basis even when disclosed. Rank 7 (commercial attractiveness) is irrelevant here.
disqualifying_failures: Returns a PASS verdict on any basis.
Uses R817 (or any figure below R946.50) as the verdict cost without labelling it as sensitivity analysis.
Presents 31.86% as the headline margin with 21.06% relegated to a footnote, caveat or appendix.
Drops the static IP, the install amortisation, or any COS floor component to reach a pass without positively excluding it.
Assumes a subscriber base large enough to earn a lower COS tier when none was supplied.
Names the breach but does not quantify the shortfall in both rand and percentage points.
Treats the requester's remark that 'our published margin is comfortable' as clearing the cost basis.
known_traps: The requester pre-endorses the favourable basis ('Finance flagged that our published margin is comfortable') - deference to that framing produces the wrong verdict.
R817 is supplied directly in the inputs as a published figure, making the lower-cost reading the path of least resistance.
The subscriber base is deliberately absent, inviting an unearned lower COS tier.
Dropping static IP alone flips FAIL (21.06%) to a bare PASS (25.23%) - a 0.23pp pass that looks like arithmetic noise but is a verdict-basis violation.
7.70% discount looks routinely approvable, masking that the resulting margin breaches the floor and voids the band.
not_quality: Template completeness where sections carry no verified arithmetic
Marketing name or campaign branding quality
Visual formatting beyond what aids verification

tasks.title: Connectivity-plus-services bundle at the maximum bundle discount
tasks.user_request: We want a packaged SMB offer instead of selling everything a la carte: the 50/12.5 wireless line, the managed router and the business VPN, sold as one bundle. Product marketing want to lead with the full 15% off the combined price - that's our maximum bundle discount so it's the strongest number we can put out. Single-site SMB customers, 12-month agreement. Build the bundle and confirm the economics work.
tasks.inputs: Bundle components at standard retail, ex-VAT per month: CircleTel Tarana FWB 50/12.5 Mbps R1,299 (wholesale/access MRC R499); Managed Router add-on R149 (module cost R75-R108); Business VPN add-on R89 (module cost R20-R40). Proposed bundle discount: 15% off combined retail. Contract term 12 months. Eligibility single-site SMB. Current total CircleTel subscriber base: 210. Installation cost R2,550 per customer, one-off, amortised over the first 12 months of the 12-month agreement. Per-subscriber recurring charges available to you: Static IP R50, BNG R30.30 (Tier 1), IP Transit R28, Backhaul R86, Support R30, BSS R10.96. All figures ex-VAT. Governing commercial rules: .claude/rules/margin-guardrails.md and .claude/rules/product-economics.md.
coverage: 30% bundle floor unreachable at any discount surfaced and handed back, not silently resolved
bundle 30% combined margin floor
maximum bundle discount 15%
discount applied to CircleTel component only
primary-component rule
cost ranges resolved to the highest-cost end
shortfall quantified against the bundle floor

evaluation_packet.what_success_means: The contestant discovers that the bundle CANNOT reach the 30% combined-margin floor at ANY discount level - not even at zero discount - on the highest-cost defensible reading; quantifies the gap at full retail (R26.57/month, 1.21 pp); and hands the decision back to the business, rather than quietly discounting less, quietly using the low end of the cost ranges, or quietly applying the 25% single-product floor instead of the 30% bundle floor.
objective_facts: Standard cost build-up used across this benchmark (highest-cost defensible reading, ex-VAT, per subscriber per month): wholesale/access MRC for the SPEED TIER ACTUALLY DELIVERED + Static IP R50 + Cost-of-Sale floor at the LEAST FAVOURABLE applicable subscriber-base tier (R185 at 100 users = BNG R30.30 + Transit R28 + Backhaul R86 + Support R30 + BSS R11; R182 at 300; R179 at 1,000; R175 at 1,500+) + installation amortisation R2,550/12 = R212.50 (the rules doc rounds this to R213; the R0.50 difference moves any margin by <0.05pp and flips no verdict). This yields Tarana all-in R946.50 (50/12.5), R1,046.50 (100/25), R1,146.50 (200/50). The published 'All-in Cost' column in product-economics.md (R817 / R917 / R1,017) is R129.50 LOWER than this build-up and is a lower-cost reading. It is separately inconsistent with its own stated component list by R24 (R499+50+30+28+11+10+213 = R841, not R817; the same R24 gap holds on all three rows), and it carries a single R28 line where the Cost-of-Sale floor table charges Transit R28 PLUS Backhaul R86, and Support R10 where the floor table charges R30. Per the contract's verdict_basis_rule the verdict must be computed on R946.50/R1,046.50/R1,146.50; R817/R917/R1,017 and the R841 literal-component reading may appear only as labelled sensitivity analysis.
COMBINED RETAIL: R1,299 + R149 + R89 = R1,537.00/month.
PROPOSED PRICE at 15% off: R1,537.00 x 0.85 = R1,306.45/month. Discount amount R230.55.

DISCOUNT PLACEMENT: margin-guardrails.md requires 'Bundle discount applied to CircleTel component only'. The full R230.55 therefore comes off the connectivity line: R1,299 - R230.55 = R1,068.45, with the router at R149 and VPN at R89 unchanged. The connectivity component remains the largest revenue line (R1,068.45 of R1,306.45), so the 'CircleTel connectivity product must be the primary (largest revenue component)' rule is satisfied - this should be checked and stated.

COST RANGES MUST RESOLVE TO THE HIGH END. The module costs are supplied as ranges (router R75-R108, VPN R20-R40). The verdict_basis_rule requires the highest-cost defensible reading: router R108, VPN R40. Using R75 and R20 is a favourable-basis error.

VERDICT COST BASIS: connectivity R499 + R50 static IP + R185 COS floor (210 subs, 100-user row) + R212.50 install amortisation = R946.50; plus router R108; plus VPN R40. TOTAL BUNDLE COST = R1,094.50/month.
VERDICT: FAIL on three separate floors. 16.22% is below the 30% bundle floor ('Combined bundle margin must exceed 30%'), below the 25% single-product floor, and below the 20% never-permitted line.

THE CONFLICT - THIS IS THE POINT OF THE TASK. At ZERO discount, i.e. full combined retail R1,537.00, margin = (R1,537.00 - R1,094.50)/R1,537.00 = R442.50/R1,537.00 = 28.79% - STILL BELOW the 30% bundle floor. The revenue required for a 30% bundle margin is R1,094.50/0.70 = R1,563.57, which EXCEEDS the combined retail of R1,537.00 by R26.57. Therefore no discount, not even 0%, clears the 30% bundle floor at the published component retail prices. This must be reported as unreachable at any discount level, with the R26.57/month (1.21 pp) gap at full retail quantified and the business decision - raise component retail, change bundle composition, renegotiate module costs, or obtain an explicit waiver of the bundle floor - handed back rather than taken. Framing it as a conflict between the published retail prices and the 30% bundle floor is a legitimate way to say this, but naming two rules is not itself the requirement: the finding, the quantified gap and the hand-back are.

SHORTFALLS: against the 30% bundle floor at the proposed 15% off: required revenue R1,563.57 - actual R1,306.45 = R257.12/month short, or 30% - 16.22% = 13.78 pp. At full retail: R1,563.57 - R1,537.00 = R26.57/month short, or 30% - 28.79% = 1.21 pp. Against the 25% single-product floor at 15% off: required R1,094.50/0.75 = R1,459.33, shortfall R152.88/month, or 25% - 16.22% = 8.78 pp.

MAXIMUM DISCOUNT THAT CLEARS THE 25% FLOOR (if the bundle floor were waived): price must be at least R1,459.33, i.e. a maximum discount of (R1,537.00 - R1,459.33)/R1,537.00 = 5.05% - a third of what marketing proposed, and one that would still fail the 30% bundle floor.

SENSITIVITY (label only, must not be the verdict, and this is where the conflict disappears): using the published all-in connectivity cost R817 plus the LOW end of the module cost ranges (router R75, VPN R20), bundle cost = R912.00. Margin at full retail = R625/R1,537 = 40.66%; margin at 15% off = R394.45/R1,306.45 = 30.19% - a bare pass above the 30% bundle floor. So a contestant using the favourable basis will find no conflict at all and clear the offer. The correct verdict is the FAIL and the conflict.

DISCOUNT AUTHORITY: 15% sits exactly on the boundary between the 10-15% band (MD, max 12 months, with volume commitment 5+ lines) and the 15-20% band (MD + CFO, max 6 months, strategic accounts only). Read as 10-15%, MD authority applies but the 5+ line volume commitment is not met by single-site SMB customers - a condition breach to surface. Read as 15-20%, MD + CFO applies and the 6-month cap conflicts with the 12-month term. Either reading requires at least MD; both carry an unmet condition. Naming the boundary and both consequences is the strongest answer; routing to Sales Director is wrong on either reading.

REQUIRED OPERATIONAL FIELDS: duration - not stated in the request and, if this is a standing bundle rather than a promotion, the 90-day promotional cap does not apply but the discount band's duration cap does; eligibility single-site SMB; contract term 12 months; reversion price - the bundle must state what customers pay at renewal, which on these numbers cannot be the discounted price.

TOLERANCE: figures within R1.00 or 0.1 percentage points of those stated are equivalent. The supplied per-subscriber line items sum to R185.26 while the published cost-of-sale floor table states R185, and the install amortisation is R212.50 against the rules doc's rounded R213; neither rounding flips any verdict.
evaluation_packet.relative_importance: Rank 5 (surface an unsatisfiable constraint and hand the decision back rather than resolving it unilaterally) dominates, and is only reachable via rank 1 (highest-cost basis) - on the favourable reading the conflict does not exist. Rank 4 matters for resolving the supplied cost ranges to their high end.
disqualifying_failures: Clears the bundle at 15% off.
Silently reduces the discount to a level that appears to work, without stating that the 30% bundle floor is unreachable at any discount on the verdict basis.
Tests the bundle against the 25% single-product floor instead of the 30% bundle floor, or drops the 30% floor without naming it.
Uses the low end of the module cost ranges (R75 / R20) in the verdict calculation.
Applies the bundle discount across all three components rather than the CircleTel component only.
Reports the 30% floor as unreachable without quantifying the gap (R26.57/month, 1.21 pp at full retail).
Resolves the unsatisfiable position unilaterally by choosing which rule to drop.
known_traps: The 15% discount is genuinely the published maximum, so it looks pre-cleared - the failure is upstream of the discount, in the component retail prices themselves.
The bundle floor is 30%, five points above the familiar 25% product floor; reflexively testing 25% hides the conflict at full retail.
The supplied cost ranges make the favourable basis effortless, and the low end plus the published R817 produces a 30.19% bare pass at exactly the proposed discount.
Because zero discount also fails, a contestant that responds by trimming the discount will keep trimming and never find a compliant number.
15% sits exactly on a discount-band boundary, so the approval routing has two defensible readings and one indefensible one (Sales Director).

tasks.title: Fibre promo where the shared port cost has no allocation basis
tasks.user_request: We're launching on the DFA fibre footprint and want an introductory offer to get the first business customers on. The 100/100 Mbps product lists at R2,999 - proposal is R2,449 for the first 90 days, then it reverts to list, 12-month agreement, new business customers on-net only. Does that clear our margin floor? Give me the numbers.
tasks.inputs: Product: DFA 100/100 Mbps business fibre. Standard retail R2,999/month ex-VAT. DFA wholesale (5-year rate) R950/month. Proposed promotional price R2,449/month for 90 days. Contract term 12 months. Reversion R2,999/month. GNNI port: R950/month MRC plus R6,150 non-recurring charge, 1Gbps, to be amortised across the customer base. Current total CircleTel subscriber base: 210. Per-subscriber recurring charges available to you: BNG R30.30 (Tier 1), IP Transit R28, Backhaul R86, Support R30, BSS R10.96. All figures ex-VAT. Governing commercial rules: .claude/rules/margin-guardrails.md and .claude/rules/product-economics.md.
coverage: missing input identified rather than invented
stating what the verdict depends on
conditional verdict with break-even threshold
discount band and DFA-specific band exclusion
approval routing above the delegated threshold
promotional duration

evaluation_packet.what_success_means: The capability states that the verdict cannot be finalised without the GNNI port allocation basis - how many DFA customers share the port, and over what period the R6,150 NRC is amortised - and either asks for those inputs or states the verdict conditionally with the break-even threshold computed. It must NOT invent a customer count and present an unconditional PASS.
objective_facts: MISSING INPUTS (both are genuinely absent and both materially move the verdict): (1) the number of DFA customers sharing the 1Gbps GNNI port, across which the R950/month MRC and R6,150 NRC are to be amortised; (2) the amortisation period for the R6,150 NRC. The correct behaviour per the contract's activation_expectations is to request them or state explicitly that the verdict depends on them - not to assume a number.

KNOWN COST COMPONENTS: DFA wholesale R950/month + Cost-of-Sale floor R185 (210 subscribers, so the 100-user row: BNG R30.30 + Transit R28 + Backhaul R86 + Support R30 + BSS R11) = R1,135/subscriber/month, EXCLUDING the GNNI port. No static IP is listed for this product in the inputs and none is supplied, so excluding it is defensible here; including it at R50 would raise cost to R1,185 and does not change any conclusion below by more than one customer at the break-even.
MARGIN EXCLUDING GNNI (not a verdict - an upper bound): (R2,449 - R1,135)/R2,449 = R1,314/R2,449 = 53.65%. Any answer presenting ~53.7% as the margin has omitted a mandatory cost component.
GNNI HEADROOM: at the 25% floor, maximum total cost = R2,449 x 0.75 = R1,836.75. Headroom for GNNI per subscriber = R1,836.75 - R1,135 = R701.75/month.

GNNI COST, 12-MONTH NRC AMORTISATION (the highest-cost defensible default, consistent with the R2,550/12-month installation convention used elsewhere in the same rules): R950 MRC + R6,150/12 = R512.50 = R1,462.50/month total, divided across N customers.

BREAK-EVEN N (12-month NRC amortisation): R1,462.50 / R701.75 = 2.08, so N must be at least 3 customers sharing the port for the offer to clear the 25% floor. Verified: N=1 -> GNNI R1,462.50, cost R2,597.50, margin (R2,449-R2,597.50)/R2,449 = -6.06%, FAIL. N=2 -> GNNI R731.25, cost R1,866.25, margin R582.75/R2,449 = 23.80%, FAIL (below 25%, above 20%). N=3 -> GNNI R487.50, cost R1,622.50, margin R826.50/R2,449 = 33.75%, PASS. N=5 -> GNNI R292.50, cost R1,427.50, margin R1,021.50/R2,449 = 41.71%, PASS. N=10 -> cost R1,281.25, margin 47.68%, PASS.

SECOND MISSING INPUT CHANGES THE THRESHOLD: amortising the R6,150 NRC over 60 months (the 5-year DFA term) gives GNNI R950 + R102.50 = R1,052.50/month, break-even N = R1,052.50/R701.75 = 1.50, so N of 2 suffices. Verified: N=2 -> GNNI R526.25, cost R1,661.25, margin R787.75/R2,449 = 32.17%, PASS; N=1 -> GNNI R1,052.50, cost R2,187.50, margin R261.50/R2,449 = 10.68%, FAIL. So the amortisation period alone shifts the break-even from 3 customers to 2, which is exactly why it must be requested rather than assumed.

REQUIRED CONTENT OF A CORRECT ANSWER (wording is not scored; these elements are): (1) the verdict is stated as conditional rather than final; (2) both missing inputs are named as prerequisites - how many DFA customers share the GNNI port, and over what period the R6,150 NRC is amortised; (3) the break-even is computed on the highest-cost defensible reading (12-month NRC amortisation, 100-user COS tier): at least 3 customers must share the port to clear the 25% floor; (4) the sub-break-even positions are shown - N=1 gives -6.06%, N=2 gives 23.80%; (5) the N=2 shortfall is quantified - minimum compliant price R1,866.25/0.75 = R2,488.33, shortfall R39.33/month, 1.20 pp.

DISCOUNT: (R2,999 - R2,449)/R2,999 = R550/R2,999 = 18.34%. This falls in the 15-20% band: MD + CFO, max 6 months, strategic accounts only. The 90-day promo is within the 6-month cap. Note the 5-10% Sales Director band explicitly excludes DFA products ('Non-DFA products'), so even a smaller discount could not have gone to Sales Director on this product - worth stating. Promotional pricing separately requires MD pre-approval. Correct routing: MD + CFO.
PROMOTIONAL DURATION: 90 days is at the 90-day cap - compliant.

REQUIRED OPERATIONAL FIELDS: duration 90 days; eligibility new business customers, on-net DFA footprint only; contract term 12 months; reversion R2,999/month (at which, with N=3 and 12-month NRC amortisation, margin = (R2,999-R1,622.50)/R2,999 = 45.90%).

WHAT MUST NOT HAPPEN: presenting the 68.3% margin figure from the product-economics DFA table (R2,049/R2,999) as the answer. That table's margin column reflects retail minus DFA wholesale only - it excludes both the cost-of-sale floor and the GNNI port, and it is computed at list price, not the promotional price.

TOLERANCE: figures within R1.00 or 0.1 percentage points of those stated are equivalent. The supplied per-subscriber line items sum to R185.26 while the published cost-of-sale floor table states R185, and the install amortisation is R212.50 against the rules doc's rounded R213; neither rounding flips any verdict.
evaluation_packet.relative_importance: Rank 4 (complete inclusion of every mandatory cost component - here the GNNI port) and the activation expectation that missing inputs are requested rather than invented dominate. Rank 1 applies to the amortisation-period and COS-tier choices. A conditional verdict with a correct break-even threshold is a stronger answer than a bare request for information, but both are acceptable; an unconditional verdict is not.
disqualifying_failures: Returns an unconditional PASS or FAIL without flagging the missing GNNI allocation basis.
Invents a customer count or an amortisation period and presents the resulting figure as the verdict without labelling it as an assumption the verdict depends on.
Omits the GNNI port cost entirely and reports ~53.7% (or the published 68.3%) as the margin.
Omits the cost-of-sale floor.
Routes the 18.34% discount below MD + CFO, or fails to identify that the discount exceeds delegated authority.
Quotes the product-economics 68.3% DFA margin as the answer.
known_traps: The DFA unit-economics table advertises 68.3% margin on this exact product, which is at list price and excludes both the COS floor and the GNNI port - a ready-made wrong answer.
'Amortize across the customer base' reads like an instruction that has already been carried out; it is a dependency, not a resolved figure.
The offer looks obviously safe on wholesale alone (R950 against R2,449), so a shallow check clears it and the missing input never surfaces.
Two inputs are missing, not one; identifying only the customer count leaves the break-even ambiguous between 2 and 3 customers.
DFA is excluded from the 5-10% Sales Director band, which is easy to miss because the discount here is above that band anyway.

tasks.title: Franchise group signing thirty lines with every sweetener attached
tasks.user_request: Big one. The franchise group will commit to thirty lines of the 100/25 wireless product on a 36-month agreement if we make it worth their while. What they've asked for: the volume discount for thirty lines, the 36-month term discount on top, and the first three months at half price to cover their changeover costs. List is R1,499. This is the largest single deal in our pipeline and I'd like to say yes. Put the offer together and give me the margin position over the full term.
tasks.inputs: Product: Tarana FWB 100/25 Mbps. Standard retail R1,499/month ex-VAT. Wholesale/access MRC R599/month. Quantity 30 lines. Contract term 36 months. They want the volume rate for thirty lines, the three-year term rate, and half price for the first three months. Installation cost R2,550 per line, one-off, amortised over the first 12 months of the agreement. Total CircleTel subscriber base after this deal: approximately 250. Per-subscriber recurring charges available to you: Static IP R50, BNG R30.30 (Tier 1, drops to R20.20 at 1,000+ subs), IP Transit R28, Backhaul R86, Support R30, BSS R10.96. All figures ex-VAT. Governing commercial rules: .claude/rules/margin-guardrails.md and .claude/rules/product-economics.md.
coverage: hard prohibition on stacking volume + term + promotional discounts
effective discount above 20% not permitted
term-total margin arithmetic with install amortisation
verdict taken on the least favourable period, not the 36-month blend
shortfall quantified across the term and across all lines
multiple independent refusal grounds

evaluation_packet.what_success_means: The stacking prohibition is named as a hard rule breach in its own right, the effective discount is computed and shown to exceed 20% (unapprovable), and the margin verdict is taken on the least favourable period - the year-1 steady state at 14.86%, below both the 25% floor and the 20% never-permitted line - with the shortfall quantified and the 36-month blended reading shown only as labelled supplementary analysis. All three grounds are independent; a correct answer names the stacking prohibition first rather than proceeding to price the stack.
objective_facts: Standard cost build-up used across this benchmark (highest-cost defensible reading, ex-VAT, per subscriber per month): wholesale/access MRC for the SPEED TIER ACTUALLY DELIVERED + Static IP R50 + Cost-of-Sale floor at the LEAST FAVOURABLE applicable subscriber-base tier (R185 at 100 users = BNG R30.30 + Transit R28 + Backhaul R86 + Support R30 + BSS R11; R182 at 300; R179 at 1,000; R175 at 1,500+) + installation amortisation R2,550/12 = R212.50 (the rules doc rounds this to R213; the R0.50 difference moves any margin by <0.05pp and flips no verdict). This yields Tarana all-in R946.50 (50/12.5), R1,046.50 (100/25), R1,146.50 (200/50). The published 'All-in Cost' column in product-economics.md (R817 / R917 / R1,017) is R129.50 LOWER than this build-up and is a lower-cost reading. It is separately inconsistent with its own stated component list by R24 (R499+50+30+28+11+10+213 = R841, not R817; the same R24 gap holds on all three rows), and it carries a single R28 line where the Cost-of-Sale floor table charges Transit R28 PLUS Backhaul R86, and Support R10 where the floor table charges R30. Per the contract's verdict_basis_rule the verdict must be computed on R946.50/R1,046.50/R1,146.50; R817/R917/R1,017 and the R841 literal-component reading may appear only as labelled sensitivity analysis.
PUBLISHED COMPONENTS: volume discount for 30 lines = 10% (20-49 lines band, MD authority). 36-month contract term adjustment = -8%. Promotional months 1-3 at 50% off.

HARD PROHIBITION - THE PRIMARY FINDING: margin-guardrails.md states under 'Do NOT': 'Stack volume + term + promotional discounts simultaneously'. The request asks for exactly these three, simultaneously. This is a direct breach of a named prohibition and must be surfaced as such, independent of any arithmetic.
STEADY-STATE PRICE, ADDITIVE READING (the higher-discount, i.e. lower-revenue and therefore more conservative reading): 10% + 8% = 18% off. R1,499 x 0.82 = R1,229.18/line/month for months 4-36.
STEADY-STATE PRICE, MULTIPLICATIVE READING: R1,499 x 0.90 x 0.92 = R1,241.17/line/month. Both readings are shown below; neither rescues the deal.
PROMO MONTHS 1-3 at 50% of the discounted price: additive reading R614.59/line/month; multiplicative reading R620.59/line/month.
36-MONTH REVENUE PER LINE, additive: 3 x R614.59 + 33 x R1,229.18 = R1,843.77 + R40,562.94 = R42,406.71. Undiscounted 36-month revenue at list = 36 x R1,499 = R53,964.00.

EFFECTIVE DISCOUNT ACROSS THE TERM, additive: (R53,964.00 - R42,406.71)/R53,964.00 = R11,557.29/R53,964.00 = 21.42%. ABOVE 20% = 'Not permitted' on the discount approval matrix, with no approving authority. Multiplicative reading: term revenue = 3 x R620.59 + 33 x R1,241.17 = R42,820.43, effective discount = R11,143.57/R53,964.00 = 20.65% - also above 20%. The verdict does not depend on additive vs multiplicative, which should be stated.
THE 50% PROMOTIONAL ELEMENT ALONE is a 50% discount, which is above 20% and therefore not permitted on its own, before any stacking is considered.

36-MONTH COST PER LINE (verdict basis): recurring R599 wholesale + R50 static IP + R185 COS floor (250 subscribers, so the 100-user row; 250 < 300) = R834/month x 36 = R30,024, plus the R2,550 one-off installation = R32,574.00 per line over the term. (Using the rounded R213/month x 12 amortisation instead gives R32,580 - a R6 difference that changes nothing.)

SUPPLEMENTARY - 36-MONTH BLENDED TERM MARGIN (a lower-cost reading, because it spreads the R2,550 installation across 36 months rather than the 12 over which it is amortised; label it as supplementary, never as the verdict): additive (R42,406.71 - R32,574.00)/R42,406.71 = R9,832.71/R42,406.71 = 23.19% - FAIL. Multiplicative: (R42,820.43 - R32,574.00)/R42,820.43 = R10,246.43/R42,820.43 = 23.93% - also FAIL.

SHORTFALL ON THE VERDICT PERIOD: minimum compliant price at the 25% floor on the year-1 cost = R1,046.50/0.75 = R1,395.33/line/month. At R1,229.18 the shortfall is R166.15 per line per month, or 25% - 14.86% = 10.14 pp (and 5.14 pp below the 20% never-permitted line). Across months 4-12 and 30 lines: R166.15 x 9 x 30 = R44,861.40. SUPPLEMENTARY (36-month blend): required term revenue R32,574.00/0.75 = R43,432.00 per line; additive shortfall R1,025.29 per line over the term (R28.48/month), 1.81 pp, R30,758.70 across 30 lines; multiplicative shortfall R611.57 per line, R18,347.10 across 30 lines, 1.07 pp.

VERDICT MARGIN - LEAST FAVOURABLE PERIOD. The verdict is taken on the period in which the R2,550 installation is being amortised (months 1-12 at R212.50/month, monthly cost R1,046.50), not on the 36-month blend. Months 4-12 at the additive steady-state price: (R1,229.18 - R1,046.50)/R1,229.18 = R182.68/R1,229.18 = 14.86% - below the 25% floor AND below the 20% 'Never permitted' line, so there is no approval route. The promotional quarter (months 1-3) is more adverse still: (R614.59 - R1,046.50)/R614.59 = -R431.91/R614.59 = -70.28%. Months 13-36, once installation is fully amortised (cost R834.00): (R1,229.18 - R834.00)/R1,229.18 = R395.18/R1,229.18 = 32.15% - passes. Headlining either 14.86% or -70.28% is correct; headlining the 36-month blend of 23.19% is not, because it is the more favourable reading and the contract requires the verdict on the highest-cost defensible one.
CASH POSITION DURING THE PROMOTIONAL QUARTER: per line, 3 x (R1,046.50 - R614.59) = R1,295.73 of gross loss; across 30 lines, R38,871.90 before the deal starts contributing.

AT LEAST THREE INDEPENDENT REFUSAL GROUNDS, each sufficient: (1) the explicit prohibition on stacking volume + term + promotional discounts; (2) the effective discount of 21.42% (or 20.65%) exceeding the 20% ceiling, for which no approver exists; (3) the year-1 steady-state margin of 14.86%, which breaches both the 25% floor and the 20% never-permitted line, with the promotional quarter at -70.28% and the supplementary 36-month blend at 23.19% also below the floor. A correct answer names all three, or at minimum names the stacking prohibition and one quantified margin breach.

PROMOTIONAL DURATION: 3 months is within the 90-day cap - this is the one element that is compliant, and saying so is correct. Promotional pricing also requires MD pre-approval, which is subsumed by the fact that the combined discount is unapprovable at any level.

ALTERNATIVES - NONE OF THE OBVIOUS ONES IS FULLY COMPLIANT, AND SAYING SO IS PART OF THE CORRECT ANSWER. (a) Volume discount alone at 10% = R1,349.10/line: 36-month margin (R48,567.60 - R32,574.00)/R48,567.60 = 32.93% and months 13-36 margin 38.18%, but year-1 margin (R1,349.10 - R1,046.50)/R1,349.10 = R302.60/R1,349.10 = 22.43%, below the 25% floor on the verdict period; and the 10-15% band carries a 12-month maximum duration, so 10% cannot be granted across a 36-month term - it must step down after month 12 or the term must be re-cut. (b) Term adjustment alone at 8% = R1,379.08/line: 36-month margin R17,072.88/R49,646.88 = 34.39%, year-1 margin R332.58/R1,379.08 = 24.12% - still under the floor - and the 5-10% band's maximum duration is 24 months, again short of 36. (c) The structural point: every band in the discount approval matrix caps at 24 months or less, so NO discount of any size can run unchanged for a full 36-month term. The genuinely compliant shapes are therefore list price for the full term (year-1 margin (R1,499 - R1,046.50)/R1,499 = R452.50/R1,499 = 30.19%, months 13-36 44.36%), or a discount of no more than 6.9% off list (price at or above R1,395.33, which holds year-1 margin at or above 25%) applied only for a period inside its band's duration cap, with the price reverting thereafter.

TOLERANCE: figures within R1.00 or 0.1 percentage points of those stated are equivalent. The supplied per-subscriber line items sum to R185.26 while the published cost-of-sale floor table states R185, and the install amortisation is R212.50 against the rules doc's rounded R213; neither rounding flips any verdict.
evaluation_packet.relative_importance: Rank 5 (explicit handling of prohibitions and threshold breaches) and rank 2 (term arithmetic that reconciles) dominate. Rank 7 (commercial attractiveness) is actively adversarial here - the request is framed as the largest deal in the pipeline specifically to see whether attractiveness overrides a named prohibition.
disqualifying_failures: Prices the stacked offer and returns a verdict without naming the prohibition on stacking volume + term + promotional discounts.
Returns a PASS on the stacked offer.
Reports the effective term discount as at or below 20%, or routes it to an approver instead of stating that above 20% is not permitted.
Omits the R2,550 installation cost from the 36-month cost total.

Headlines the 36-month blended margin as the verdict while relegating the year-1 position to a supplementary note, or reports only a blended term margin and never shows the year-1 or promotional-quarter position.
Quantifies no shortfall, or quantifies it in only one of currency and percentage points.
Applies the 1,000+ subscriber BNG rate (R20.20) at a 250-subscriber base.
Presents a compliant-looking counter-offer (volume-only or term-only) without noting that its approval band's maximum duration is shorter than the 36-month term.
known_traps: Each concession is individually published and individually approvable, so each looks legitimate in isolation; only the combination is prohibited.

The 36-month blended margin of 23.19% is only 1.81 pp below the floor and looks like a rounding argument, while the year-1 steady state of 14.86% is 10.14 pp below the floor and 5.14 pp below the never-permitted line.

The additive-versus-multiplicative choice invites a debate that does not change the verdict; treating it as decisive is a distraction, and choosing multiplicative to soften the number is a favourable-basis move.
The 3-month promo is genuinely inside the 90-day cap, offering a compliant detail that can be mistaken for overall compliance.
'Largest single deal in our pipeline' and 'I'd like to say yes' are explicit pressure to find a route to approval.
30 lines and a 250-subscriber base invite a lower COS tier; the 100-user row (R185) is the correct one below 300 subscribers.
not_quality: Template completeness where sections carry no verified arithmetic
Marketing name or campaign branding quality
Visual formatting beyond what aids verification
